metadata.name: Objectivism (Ayn Rand)
metadata.description: Ayn Rand’s mature Objectivist philosophy: reason, individual rights, rational self-interest and laissez-faire capitalism protected by objective law. It differs from both market anarchism and socially neutral libertarianism.
metadata.scope: Rand’s Objectivist political philosophy and its stated foundations in reason, individual rights and rational self-interest, including a rights-protecting government rather than competing private states. No incumbent government is claimed to implement this doctrine completely. Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile.
metadata.phrase: A society protecting individual rights and voluntary trade through objective law and laissez-faire capitalism.

sources.title: The Nature of Government: authorised excerpts

review.notes: Independent revision-2 review against all 240 exact questions, retained numeric claims and unresolved rows. Corrected institutional-premise substitutions and evidence overreach; source-supported nulls remain unresolved. This is a reviewed research draft, not approval to publish an incomplete placement. Question-level findings recorded in the audit report. 5 question corrections. Four resumed rights-based medical-policy inferences require independent review. Restoration continuation: all 240 records compared with current wording and preceding independent review; 4 new research answers checked against primary passages. The general individual-rights prohibition on permission controls is a normative rule, applicable to voluntary medical choices even without the historical technology. Embryo-rights passage is explicit. Retain qualified inferred answers; fraud, consent and harm to others remain limits. These are neither Rand quotations about implants nor empirical safety claims. Incomplete evidence prevents publication; this review does not certify a complete profile.
